newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Victoria seen reaping A$4.86 bln for Loy Yang A.
newsitem.headline: Victoria seen reaping A$4.86 bln for Loy Yang A.

text.p: The Victoria state government will announce at 0230 GMT (12.30 p.m.) the sale of its Loy Yang A power station for an expected headline price of about A$4.86 billion, making it Australia's biggest single privatisation, sources said on Tuesday.
A consortium comprising CMS Energy Corp, NRG Energy Inc and Horizon Energy Investments Ltd are known to have been chosen as buyer with a core bid of A$4.75 billion.

Other consortia bidding for the 2,000 megawatt power station and associated brown coal mine, producing 30 million tonnes a year, were led by U.S. utilities American Electric Power Co Inc and AES Corp.
The sale price announced by the government is likely to be higher than the A$4.75 billion winning bid for the assets, a corporate source told Reuters.

The headline price announced would be around A$4.86 billion, including the additional price paid by winning consortium for coal sale contracts relating to a pulverising coal processing plant at the Loy Yang A site, east of Melbourne.
The contracts were worth around A$109 million, he said.
"There's a benefit to the state from the assumption of those contracts, but it's not a part of the pricie for the assets," the source said.

The Victoria state government, rated AA-plus for its domestic long-term debt, has so far sold over A$13 billion worth of electricity assets in its drive to slash debt and seek a top credit rating of AAA.
